# TITLE 7. SSH SERVER HARDENING # SUBTITLE LINUX SECURITY HANDBOOK # BADGES PAGE 7 OF 20 # SECTION_HEADINGS - SSH ATTACK SURFACE - KEY-BASED AUTHENTICATION - DISABLING ROOT SSH LOGIN - DISABLING PASSWORD AUTHENTICATION - SSHD_CONFIG - RESTRICTING USERS AND GROUPS - SSH KEY PERMISSIONS - IDLE-SESSION CONTROLS - TESTING CONFIGURATION BEFORE RESTART - REVIEWING SSH AUTHENTICATION LOGS - IMPORTANT SSHD_CONFIG SETTINGS - SSH KEY GENERATION (ON CLIENT) - COPY PUBLIC KEY TO SERVER - VALIDATE SSH CONFIGURATION - RELOAD SSH SERVICE - REVIEW AUTHENTICATION LOGS # BODY_PARAGRAPHS **SSH ATTACK SURFACE** SSH is a common target for attackers. Reduce exposure by limiting access, strengthening authentication, and monitoring activity. **KEY-BASED AUTHENTICATION** Use SSH keys instead of passwords. Stronger, more secure, and resistant to brute-force attacks. **DISABLING ROOT SSH LOGIN** Do not allow root to login via SSH. Use a regular user and sudo for administrative tasks. **DISABLING PASSWORD AUTHENTICATION** Disable password-based login. Prevents brute-force and credential stuffing attacks. **SSHD_CONFIG** Main SSH server configuration file. Harden settings in /etc/ssh/sshd_config and reload SSH service safely. **RESTRICTING USERS AND GROUPS** Allow only specific users or groups to access SSH. Deny all others. **SSH KEY PERMISSIONS** Private key (id_rsa): 600 Public key (id_rsa.pub): 644 ~/.ssh directory: 700 authorized_keys file: 600 Wrong permissions = login failure. **IDLE-SESSION CONTROLS** Set timeouts for idle sessions. Disconnect inactive sessions automatically to reduce risk. **TESTING CONFIGURATION BEFORE RESTART** Always validate SSH configuration before restarting to avoid lockout. Use test mode: sshd -t **REVIEWING SSH AUTHENTICATION LOGS** Monitor SSH login attempts, failed logins, and suspicious activity regularly. Logs help detect brute-force attacks early. # IMPORTANT_FILES | File Path | Description | | :--- | :--- | | /etc/ssh/sshd_config | Main SSH server configuration file. Harden settings here and reload SSH service safely. | | ~/.ssh/id_rsa | Private key file. Requires permissions of 600. | | ~/.ssh/id_rsa.pub | Public key file. Requires permissions of 644. | | ~/.ssh | User's SSH directory. Requires permissions of 700. | | ~/.ssh/authorized_keys | File storing authorized public keys. Requires permissions of 600. | | /var/log/auth.log | Log file containing authentication logs and login attempts. | # TABLES ## IMPORTANT SSHD_CONFIG SETTINGS | Setting | Value | | :--- | :--- | | Port | 22 | | Protocol | 2 | | PermitRootLogin | no | | PasswordAuthentication | no | | ChallengeResponseAuthentication | no | | UsePAM | yes | | AllowUsers | user1 user2 | | AllowGroups | sshusers | | X11Forwarding | no | | MaxAuthTries | 3 | | LoginGraceTime | 30s | | ClientAliveInterval | 300 | | ClientAliveCountMax | 2 | # COMMANDS | Command | Description | Example | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `ssh-keygen` | Generates a new SSH key pair on the client machine. | `ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "your_email@domain.com" -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519` | | `ssh-copy-id` | Copies the public key to the remote server's authorized_keys file. | `ssh-copy-id -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub user@server_ip` | | `cat` (with pipe) | Alternative method to copy the public key to the server by creating the directory and appending the key. | `cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub \| ssh user@server_ip "mkdir -p ~/.ssh && cat >> ~/.ssh/authorized_keys"` | | `sshd -t` | Validates the SSH configuration syntax without restarting the service. | `sshd -t` | | `sudo systemctl reload sshd` | Reloads the SSH daemon to apply configuration changes without dropping existing connections. | `sudo systemctl reload sshd` | | `sudo systemctl restart sshd` | Restarts the SSH daemon completely if a reload is not sufficient. | `sudo systemctl restart sshd` | | `sudo journalctl` | Views system logs, specifically filtering for SSH service entries since a specific time. | `sudo journalctl -u ssh --since "1 hour ago"` | | `sudo grep` | Searches authentication log files for specific keywords like "sshd" or "Failed password". | `sudo grep "sshd" /var/log/auth.log`
`sudo grep "Failed password" /var/log/auth.log` | # TIPS_NOTES_WARNINGS - **Note:** If `sshd -t` produces no output, the configuration is valid. - **Warning:** If errors are found during validation, fix them before restarting the service to avoid being locked out. - **Tip:** Use `sudo systemctl reload sshd` to apply changes, or restart if necessary. # PRACTICAL_EXERCISES *(No explicit numbered practical exercise steps are present on this page; the commands and configurations serve as the procedural guide.)* # FOOTER_TEXT VERIQTA YouTube @veriqta GitHub @veriqta LinkedIn @veriqta X @veriqta Instagram @veriqta Telegram @veriqta # PAGE_NUMBER PAGE 7 OF 20
